financial_additionality_project_cost_bre.description: An itemised breakdown of all costs associated with implementing and operating the project, including both capital expenditure (CapEx) and operational expenditure (OpEx), used as an input to the financial additionality analysis.

financial_additionality_project_revenue_.description: An itemised breakdown of all revenue streams generated by the project other than carbon credit revenue, including product or service sales, cost savings, and public subsidies or grants, used as an input to the financial additionality analysis.

financial_additionality_financial_indica.description: The financial metric selected to assess the project's financial viability (e.g. net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), or benefit-cost ratio), applied consistently throughout the financial additionality calculations.

financial_additionality_financial_benchm.description: The underlying calculations used to derive the project's financial indicator for comparison against the chosen financial benchmark, including all assumptions, inputs, and formulas used.

financial_additionality_investment_analy.description: Indicates which financial investment analysis method is used to assess additionality: simple cost analysis, investment comparison analysis, or benchmark analysis.

financial_additionality_investment_compa.description: The calculations comparing the financial performance (e.g. IRR or NPV) of the project against one or more realistic alternative investment options, used to support the investment comparison analysis.

financial_additionality_financial_benchm.description: The outcome of comparing the project's financial indicator against the chosen financial benchmark, together with the justification for why this outcome shows the project is not financially viable without carbon credit revenue.

financial_additionality_investment_compa.description: The outcome of the investment comparison analysis, which assesses whether the project is less economically attractive than one or more alternative investment options. If the project would not be chosen over more financially viable alternatives without carbon credit revenue, it may be considered additional.

financial_additionality_sensitivity_anal.description: The outcome of testing how the project's financial viability conclusion changes when key assumptions (e.g. costs, revenues, discount rate) are varied within a reasonable range, demonstrating whether the conclusion is robust.
Supporting evidence and documentation for the sensitivity analysis, including the assumptions tested, the ranges applied, and the sources used to justify those ranges.

financial_additionality_simple_cost_anal.description: Details of the simple cost analysis, a financial additionality test that compares a project's expected costs and revenues to determine if it would be economically unattractive without carbon credit income. If the project would not generate sufficient returns, or would operate at a loss, without the added revenue from credits, it may be deemed additional.

Supporting evidence and documentation for the simple cost analysis, including the cost and revenue data sources and calculations used to determine that the project would be financially unattractive without carbon credit revenue.

financial_additionality_carbon_finance_d.description: Evidence demonstrating that the project's implementation is contingent on, or directly enabled by, carbon credit revenue (e.g. financial modelling, board minutes, or investment decisions referencing carbon finance).

financial_additionality_sensitivity_anal.description: Indicates whether a sensitivity analysis has been conducted to show whether the conclusion regarding financial attractiveness is robust to reasonable variation in the critical assumptions.

financial_additionality_low_capex_relati.description: Indicates whether the project has no other significant income streams and/or minimal capital expenditure relative to operational expenditure — a condition under which a simplified cost analysis, rather than IRR/NPV benchmarking, may be used to demonstrate financial additionality.

financial_additionality_direct_result_of.description: Indicates whether the project is not financially feasible, or is less financially attractive than alternative activities, in the absence of carbon credit revenue.

financial_additionality_financial_benchm.description: Indicates whether a benchmark approach is used, comparing the project's expected return (e.g. IRR or NPV) to a predefined financial benchmark. If the project's return falls below this benchmark without carbon credit revenue, it may be considered financially additional.

financial_additionality_carbon_revenue_d.description: Indicates whether carbon credit revenue is the decisive factor in overcoming an identified implementation barrier (e.g. financial, technical, regulatory, or market-related) that would otherwise prevent the project from being implemented.

barriers_alternative_scenario_barrier_de.description: Demonstration that at least one plausible alternative to the project does not face the same significant barriers as the project itself.

barriers_barrier_demonstration.description: Evidence to (i) demonstrate each barrier identified as preventing the project's implementation, and (ii) show that carbon credit revenue is the key factor in overcoming each barrier.

barriers_chosen_barrier_explanation_and_.description: Explanation of the specific barrier(s) selected for the barrier analysis and the results demonstrating that carbon credit revenue is the decisive factor in overcoming them.

barriers_implementation_barriers.description: Indicates which type of barrier analysis is conducted. Examples include: financial barriers, institutional barriers, information barriers, and other barriers specific to the project and/or the region where it is implemented, provided these are explicitly identified and elaborated in the relevant quantification methodology or other programme documents.

barriers_other_additionality_approach_na.description: The name of the standardised additionality approach used, where the project relies on an approach other than financial, barrier, or common practice analysis (e.g. a programme-specific or methodology-specific tool).

barriers_other_barrier_types.description: Description of any barrier type(s) faced by the project that fall outside the standard categories (e.g. financial, institutional, technological, information), including how these barriers were identified and assessed.

common_practice_common_practice_document.description: Supporting evidence and documentation for the common practice analysis, including the data sources used to identify comparable projects or activities and to calculate the level of market penetration.

common_practice_common_practice_test_det.description: Overview of the approach used to determine additionality and the methodology, carbon-crediting programme, or equivalent entity responsible for setting the threshold for market penetration.

common_practice_first_of_kind_details.description: Details and justification demonstrating that the project's mitigation activity is the first of its kind, including how it differs from existing practices or technologies within the relevant sector and/or region.

common_practice_first_of_kind.description: Indicates whether the project's mitigation activity implements an innovative approach or technology that sets it apart from existing practices or solutions within a given sector or region.

common_practice_first_of_kind_documentat.description: Supporting evidence and documentation substantiating the project's claim to be a first-of-its-kind mitigation activity.

common_practice_passes_common_practice_t.description: Indicates whether the project passes the common practice or market penetration test, which evaluates whether a mitigation activity is already widely adopted in a sector or region. If the activity is already standard practice, it is not considered additional and is ineligible for carbon credits.

common_practice_market_penetration_thres.description: The threshold or maximum level of market penetration or adoption below which a mitigation activity is not considered common practice, as defined by the applicable methodology or carbon-crediting programme.

counterfactual_scenario_counterfactual_s.description: A summary of the counterfactual scenario outlining what would likely have occurred in the absence of carbon finance. CO2 removals or reductions are considered additional only when measured against a conservative baseline representing this alternative scenario.
Supporting documentation for the counterfactual analysis, based on baselines that are project-specific, conservative, and periodically updated.
The counterfactual(s), or alternative scenario(s), describing what would plausibly happen if the mitigation activity did not occur.

counterfactual_scenario_exceeds_emission.description: Indicates whether the project's mitigation activity achieves emission reductions and/or removals beyond the applicable performance benchmark, a requirement for demonstrating additionality under a performance-based approach.

counterfactual_scenario_alternative_scen.description: Supporting evidence and documentation for the alternative scenario barrier analysis, demonstrating that identified alternatives to the project do not face the same barriers as the project.

general_additionality_approaches_used.description: The additionality approach(es) applied to the project (e.g. financial additionality, barrier analysis, common practice test, performance-based approach), used to ensure carbon credits are granted only to activities that would not have occurred without the incentive provided by carbon credit revenue.

general_credits_considered_before_start_.description: Indicates whether carbon revenue was considered or planned for prior to the project's start date. Evidence of such "prior consideration" helps demonstrate that the project would not have been developed without the financial incentive from carbon credits.

general_standardized_additionality_resul.description: The outcome of applying the chosen standardised additionality approach (e.g. a positive list, performance benchmark, or activity-specific tool), including the conclusion reached on the project's additionality status.

general_prior_consideration_details.description: Details of when and how carbon credit revenue was considered or planned for prior to the project's start date, including relevant dates and decisions.

general_prior_consideration_evidence.description: Supporting evidence substantiating that carbon credit revenue was considered prior to the project's start date (e.g. feasibility studies, board approvals, letters of intent, or correspondence with buyers or registries dated before the start date).

general_other_additionality_evidence.description: Supporting evidence for any additionality measure(s) used by the project that are not covered by the standard financial, barrier, common practice, or performance-based approaches.

general_uses_other_standardized_approach.description: Indicates whether the project uses a standardised approach, other than financial, barrier, or common practice analysis, to demonstrate additionality.

lockin_risk_applicable_activities_techno.description: The activities and/or technologies to which the standardised additionality approach applies. The approach must be defined at an appropriate level of aggregation of technologies/activities and at a high level of stringency.

lockin_risk_country_ltleds_compatibility.description: Assessment of whether the project's technology or activity is compatible with the host country's Long-Term Low-Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS) and decarbonisation pathway, used to evaluate the risk that the project locks in high-emission infrastructure or practices.

lockin_risk_project_scale.description: The scale of the project (e.g. capacity, output, or size classification), used to assess lock-in risk, since larger-scale, longer-lived assets can pose a greater risk of locking in emissions-intensive infrastructure or practices.

lockin_risk_technology_emissions_intensi.description: The emissions intensity of the technology or activity implemented by the project, relative to lower-carbon alternatives, used to assess the risk that the project locks in higher-emitting technology over its operational lifetime.

performance_additionality_performance_ba.description: The outcome of the performance-based additionality assessment, showing how the project's actual emission reductions and/or removals compare against the applicable performance threshold or benchmark.

Supporting evidence and documentation for the performance-based additionality assessment, including the data and methodology used to measure the project's performance against the applicable benchmark.

performance_additionality_performance_in.description: Description of the specific performance indicator (e.g. emissions per unit of output) used to measure the project's performance against the applicable performance-based additionality benchmark.

performance_additionality_performance_th.description: Description of the performance threshold or benchmark value that the project's performance indicator must meet or exceed to demonstrate additionality under the performance-based approach.
The period for which the applicable performance threshold or benchmark remains valid before it must be reviewed or updated (e.g. in line with methodology or programme review cycles).

regulatory_additionality_regulatory_surp.description: Overview of the applicable laws and regulations used to justify regulatory additionality, by demonstrating that the mitigation activity is not legally required.

regulatory_additionality_legal_regulator.description: Supporting documentation demonstrating that the project's mitigation activity is not mandated by, and/or exceeds the requirements of, applicable laws, regulations, or other binding obligations.

regulatory_additionality_exceeds_legal_r.description: Indicates whether the project's mitigation activity goes beyond what is required by existing applicable laws, regulations, or other binding obligations — a condition for demonstrating regulatory additionality.

regulatory_additionality_regulatory_addi.description: The method used to determine regulatory additionality (e.g. legal analysis of applicable laws and regulations, assessment of enforcement levels, or a positive list of activities), as specified by the applicable methodology or carbon-crediting programme.
